problem: Reinforcement learning policies for reasoning collapse when positive sharpening and negative squeezing create irreversible contraction in the sampling probability of valid alternatives.
approach: Anchored Policy Optimization (APO) shifts from global shape-matching constraints to support coverage, using a safe manifold based on reference model confidence to permit aggressive sharpening while selectively invoking restorative forces during error correction.
contribution: APO breaks the accuracy-diversity trade-off by maintaining support coverage and improving both Pass@1 correctness and Pass@K diversity on mathematical benchmarks.

problem: Identifying root causes in complex microservice systems requires navigating intricate dependencies that exceed human expertise, and existing causal methods are sample-inefficient without full causal graphs.
approach: Bayesian Root Cause Discovery (BRCD) leverages partial causal structure via CPDAGs and uniform DAG sampling to perform Bayesian inference efficiently without enumerating all interventional Markov equivalence classes.
contribution: BRCD provides the first statistical consistency guarantees for nonparametric RCA with identifiability and finite-sample posterior bounds, achieving state-of-the-art top-l accuracy on microservice benchmarks.

problem: In decentralized social learning where each agent controls a short episode of decisions, exploration systematically fails and Bayesian regret grows linearly despite per-agent incentives to explore.
approach: Analyze a stylized multi-armed bandit protocol where self-interested agents collectively exhibit aggregate exploration failure even with diverse per-round utilities (min, max, sum).
contribution: The paper demonstrates that exploration failure is typical in episodic social learning, proving that externally driven exploration is necessary even when local exploration occurs organically.

problem: Predicting periodic charge densities in crystalline materials is computationally expensive due to explicit real-space grid probing and periodic image summation in traditional methods.
approach: ELECTRAFI constructs anisotropic Gaussians in real space and uses their closed-form Fourier transforms via the Poisson summation formula to analytically evaluate plane-wave coefficients with a single inverse FFT.
contribution: ELECTRAFI matches or exceeds state-of-the-art accuracy while being up to 633x faster than competing methods, reducing total DFT compute cost by approximately 20% when used to initialize calculations.

problem: Black-box agentic systems remain difficult to interpret and control because their internal workflows are opaque, limiting user understanding and editability.
approach: AgentXRay formulates Agentic Workflow Reconstruction (AWR) as a combinatorial optimization problem using Monte Carlo Tree Search with Red-Black Pruning to synthesize interpretable stand-in workflows that approximate black-box systems via input-output access.
contribution: AgentXRay produces editable white-box workflows matching target outputs without model parameters, achieving higher proxy similarity and reduced token consumption compared to unpruned search.

problem: Time series foundation models process temporal patterns through single-pass inference but regional climate prediction requires multi-scale temporal analysis and iterative refinement like expert climatologists employ.
approach: RGMR (Residual-Guided Multi-Resolution Refinement) performs structured coarse-to-fine refinement at inference-time via residual guidance without updating backbone parameters, working across multiple TSFM architectures.
contribution: RGMR reduces test-set MSE on SPEI drought forecasting by up to 18.9% across South Australian sites with consistent improvements on TimesFM, TimeGPT, and TabPFN architectures.

problem: Vision-Language Models suffer from the Likelihood Trap where standard alignment objectives (MLE, KL-regularization) drive generation toward generic high-probability templates, suppressing fine-grained visual details.
approach: Geo-RL reformulates caption generation from probabilistic likelihood to geometric coverage maximization via Determinantal Point Processes, enforcing orthogonality among descriptions to span the image's full semantic support.
contribution: Geo-RL escapes the likelihood trap, achieving significant improvements in semantic richness and detail coverage without compromising visual grounding.

problem: Designing RNA sequences that fold into specific secondary structures remains computationally challenging because the inverse design problem has high complexity and poor exploration of design policies.
approach: CocoRNA decomposes RNA inverse design into smaller sub-problems solved collaboratively by multiple agents using cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, with a centralized critic using global structural information.
contribution: CocoRNA substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in success rate and design speed on the Rfam dataset, with policies that generalize to unseen structures without additional training.

problem: Web agents require massive trajectories to generalize but real-world training is constrained by network latency, rate limits, and safety risks, necessitating efficient simulation.
approach: WebWorld series leverages a scalable data pipeline to train on 1M+ open-web interactions, supporting reasoning and multi-format data via a differentiable simulator enabling 30+ step long-horizon simulations.
contribution: WebWorld achieves simulation performance comparable to Gemini-3-Pro; Qwen3-14B trained on WebWorld-synthesized trajectories improves +9.2% on WebArena reaching GPT-4o performance levels.

problem: Learning-augmented paging algorithms have a robustness gap; prior work achieves 2H_k + O(1) competitive ratio but the optimal ratio is H_k, leaving room for improvement.
approach: Introduce the relative prediction budget as a unifying primitive to analyze robustness in learning-augmented paging, developing a framework that closes the gap between theoretical optimality and practical performance.
contribution: Achieve the best-possible robustness of H_k + O(1) competitive ratio for learning-augmented paging with strong practical performance demonstrated experimentally.

problem: Large Multimodal Models have static, limited knowledge that cannot keep pace with real-world developments, leading to the challenge of continuous knowledge acquisition while preventing catastrophic forgetting.
approach: KORE implements KnOwledge-oRientEd controls via a two-stage process: automatic conversion of knowledge items into structured forms for accurate learning, and storage of previous knowledge in covariance matrices while initializing adapters in the null space to minimize interference.
contribution: KORE achieves superior new knowledge injection and effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting across LLaVA-v1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL models.

problem: Adversarial attacks against closed-source MLLMs face a transferability problem because methods that maximize latent representation similarity overfit to specific targets with poor generalization.
approach: DART adopts a statistical lens using Energy Distance to characterize intrinsic image semantics for distribution-aware alignment, and trains a GNN to adaptively select surrogate models that maximize transferability.
contribution: DART demonstrates superior robustness and effectiveness in adversarial attacks against closed-source MLLMs compared to competing baselines.

problem: Reconstructing complete yet compact 3D Gaussian Splatting representations from sparse-view monocular video is challenged by correlated pseudo-views and repeated merging that accumulate structured, non-i.i.d. redundancy.
approach: CoverPruneGS implements coverage-preserving structured pruning via coarse-to-fine voxel-based diversity selection and ground-truth-guided lazy refinement with footprint-aware CUDA attribution for precise importance scoring.
contribution: CoverPruneGS reduces Gaussian counts by 56.8%, significantly accelerates inference, and enhances or maintains novel view synthesis quality across multiple datasets.

problem: Modeling Koopman dynamics for nonlinear systems is computationally burdensome due to sequential propagation that creates a linear-depth temporal composition bottleneck.
approach: Use Lie-algebraic structure to constrain neural generators within prescribed Lie subalgebras and construct finite-time flows via neural Magnus expansion, applying prefix-scan algorithms to reduce composition depth from linear to logarithmic.
contribution: The framework enables accurate long-horizon prediction while improving computational efficiency through scalable Koopman operator learning for nonlinear systems.

problem: scRNA-seq clustering using graph transformers has O(n^2) computational and space complexity, limiting applicability to large-scale single-cell RNA datasets.
approach: BGFormer introduces learnable anchor tokens as shared reference points and uses bipartite graph attention to learn similarity between cells and anchors, achieving linear computational complexity.
contribution: BGFormer achieves state-of-the-art clustering performance with linear complexity, demonstrating effectiveness and scalability on multiple large-scale scRNA-seq datasets.

problem: Multi-agent reinforcement learning under partial observability struggles to specify complex objectives and constraints without formal specification frameworks.
approach: HyPOLE integrates formal specifications via HyperLTL temporal logic with Centralized Training for Decentralized Execution (CTDE) to synthesize decentralized policies guided by expressive hyperproperties.
contribution: HyPOLE demonstrates clear advantages over baselines on SMAC, MessySMAC, and WildFire benchmarks for learning formally-specified multi-agent behaviors.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models require substantial task-specific demonstrations for adaptation, but action imitation ignores richer trajectory structure that could improve few-shot adaptation.
approach: DynVLA reformulates VLA learning from action imitation to motion dynamics modeling, using Motion Dynamics Mechanism (MDM) to distill latent embeddings via flow-matching inversion and projecting onto a Dynamics Bank of prior motion knowledge.
contribution: DynVLA outperforms SOTA by 15.8% in average success rate with around 20 demonstrations on 13 real-world manipulation tasks.

problem: Large-scale web-crawled datasets contain noise and bias but existing data-selection methods depend on hand-crafted heuristics, downstream datasets, or expensive influence computations.
approach: Mimic Score measures alignment between a sample's gradients and a target direction induced by a pre-trained reference model, with Grad-Mimic framework providing online re-weighting and offline filtering stages.
contribution: Mimic scores guide training to improve data efficiency and accelerate convergence with consistent gains across six image datasets; CLIP models trained with 4.7M fewer samples show improved performance.

problem: Web agents fine-tuned on specific trajectories and domains struggle to generalize out-of-domain, and offline training is compute-inefficient due to noisy, redundant trajectories and long accessibility-tree states.
approach: Weasel selects a fixed-budget trajectory subset by optimizing importance-diversity objectives over states, websites, and interaction patterns via greedy algorithms, with target-centered AXTree pruning and style-consistent rationale replacement.
contribution: Weasel improves out-of-domain performance with roughly 9.7-12.5x training speedups over standard fine-tuning across WebArena, WorkArena, and MiniWob benchmarks.

problem: Gastrointestinal motility assessment via bowel sounds is compromised by spectral overlap with non-stationary speech interference, and traditional Gaussian-based diffusion frameworks struggle with impulsive, heavy-tailed clinical noise.
approach: Propose Cauchy-driven Diffusion Bridge framework with closed-form score and density expressions derived to model heavy-tailed perturbations, implementing efficient sampling via Gaussian scale-mixture reparameterization.
contribution: Framework achieves state-of-the-art performance outperforming baselines by 13.4-49.8% across metrics, elevating abnormal bowel sound recognition accuracy to 88.01% on a large clinical dataset (25+ hours).

problem: Population dynamics inference typically focuses on gradient flows that minimize kinetic energy, but this selection criterion may not capture non-potential transport mechanisms present in real systems.
approach: Non-Gradient Inference Flows (NGIF) leverages gauge freedom to infer general vector fields using weak formulation of continuity equation, enabling parameterization with alternative selection criteria beyond minimal energy.
contribution: NGIF improves distributional accuracy over gradient-restricted baselines and better captures non-potential transport on low- and high-dimensional physics problems.

problem: In-Context Reinforcement Learning's efficacy in Ad-Hoc Teamwork with unknown partners remains unexplored, requiring rigorous evaluation with diverse teammate suites and train-test shifts.
approach: Introduce ICRL4AHT benchmark built on high-throughput JAX Overcooked-V2 with diverse teammate suite and reproducible pipeline for teammate generation, dataset construction, and evaluation.
contribution: Evaluation reveals that representative ICRL algorithms (AD, DPT) fail to exhibit robust test-time adaptation in multi-agent settings, underperforming random baselines across unseen teammates and layouts.

problem: Evidential Deep Learning can be overconfident and poorly calibrated while failing to represent multi-modal epistemic uncertainty despite single-pass inference capability.
approach: Gated Evidential Mixtures (GEM) learns an in-model energy signal to gate evidential outputs end-to-end; GEM-MIX adds mixture of evidential heads with learned routing; GEM-FI stabilizes via Fisher-informed regularization.
contribution: GEM improves calibration and ID/OOD separation with single-pass inference; GEM-FI improves CIFAR-10 accuracy from 91.11% to 93.75% and reduces Brier score substantially.

problem: Prototype-based few-shot point cloud semantic segmentation fails to adequately model feature distribution shift between support and query sets, resulting in insufficient prototype adaptation.
approach: DPR-Net constructs progressive adaptation via coarse-to-fine prototype evolution, decomposing features into common and distinctive subspaces to enable targeted adjustment while preserving class-shared semantics.
contribution: DPR-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance on few-shot point cloud semantic segmentation with high efficiency and provides code availability.

problem: One-shot skeleton-based action recognition requires capturing hierarchical and compositional human motion structure while aligning with action semantics under extreme data scarcity.
approach: SkelHCC embeds skeleton sequences and action language into a shared hyperbolic space via Explicitly Hierarchical Hyperbolic CLIP (EH-HCLIP), leveraging hyperbolic geometry to encode anatomical hierarchy; LLM-guided Multi-granularity Voting Cache enables training-free adaptation.
contribution: SkelHCC outperforms state-of-the-art methods on NTU RGB+D 60/120 and PKU-MMD II datasets for one-shot action recognition.

problem: Recovering scene-consistent 4D crowd motion from monocular video in large-scale scenes is challenged by severe depth ambiguity and complex scene geometry with typical single-plane assumptions leading to unreliable metric scale.
approach: Crowd4D jointly optimizes crowd and scene via Human-Scene Interaction Proxy (HSIP) derived from Scene Interaction Point Clouds and Surface, with Crowd Structural Coherence Regularization (CSCR) to improve temporal stability under occlusions.
contribution: Crowd4D consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods for robust monocular 4D crowd reconstruction in complex, large-scale scenes.

problem: EEG foundation models inadequately model complex spatiotemporal topology and suffer from modality gap between low-level physiological signals and high-level textual semantics.
approach: KAST-BAR dynamically aligns physiological representations from multi-level brain topology with expert-level semantic space via Dual-Stream Hierarchical Attention (DSHA) encoder and Knowledge-Anchored Semantic Profiler (KASP), with Semantic Text-Aware Refiner (STAR).
contribution: KAST-BAR achieves state-of-the-art performance across six downstream tasks through large-scale pre-training on 21 diverse EEG datasets.

problem: Multimodal visual tracking requires training separate models for each modality or relying on pretrained models, limiting efficiency, scalability, and usability for unified multi-modal approaches.
approach: OneTrackerV2 introduces Meta Merger to embed multi-modal information into unified space; Dual Mixture-of-Experts (DMoE) models spatiotemporal relations (T-MoE) and multi-modal knowledge (M-MoE) with shared architecture and unified parameters.
contribution: OneTrackerV2 achieves state-of-the-art performance across five RGB and RGB+X tracking tasks with 12 benchmarks while maintaining high inference efficiency and strong performance under modality-missing scenarios.

problem: Standard expected-reward RL formulation is only a first-order approximation of maximum likelihood when feedback is terminal and binary, leading to suboptimal sample efficiency.
approach: Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (MaxRL) introduces a compute-indexed family of sample-based objectives that interpolate between expected-reward RL and maximum likelihood as sampling compute scales.
contribution: MaxRL Pareto-dominates existing methods, achieves up to 20x gains in test-time scaling efficiency over GRPO, and scales more favorably with additional training data and compute.

problem: Influence functions for data debugging and unlearning become impractical for high-query subset workloads like large-K cross-validation due to expensive inverse-curvature solves required per query.
approach: Clustered Influence Functions (CiF) amortizes subset influence computation by clustering training gradients once, solving damped Generalised Gauss-Newton only for cluster means, and answering queries via linear recombination using cluster membership counts.
contribution: CiF matches per-query influence rankings while significantly reducing total runtime in high-Q regimes, enabling influence-based workflows that are otherwise computationally prohibitive.

problem: Scaling inference-time computation through parallel reasoning in LLMs suffers from performance degradation compared to sequential counterparts and often requires specialized inference engines.
approach: ThreadWeaver enables adaptive parallel reasoning via a two-stage parallel trajectory generator for supervised fine-tuning, trie-based rollout for any off-the-shelf autoregressive engine, and parallelization-aware RL framework.
contribution: ThreadWeaver matches sequential reasoning accuracy (79.9% on AIME24, 71.9% average) while delivering up to 1.53x speedup in token latency on Qwen3-8B.

problem: Graph Transformers lack a unified theoretical understanding of desirable propagation operators despite diverse topology injection paradigms.
approach: BDFormer rethinks Graph Transformers from a graph signal denoising perspective with block-diagonal structure as a desirable prior, imposing spectral block regularization on compact anchor affinities and using hard assignments for sparse propagation.
contribution: BDFormer establishes superior performance and scalability by achieving block-diagonal propagation structure with linear-time complexity.

problem: Standard value function learning in reinforcement learning lacks geometric structure that could stabilize and accelerate learning by encoding symmetries and constraints.
approach: GCR-RL (Geometric Coherence Regularized RL) recasts value function learning through order theory as learning a desired poset, computing sequences of super-poset refinements via temporal difference signals while ensuring geometric coherence.
contribution: GCR-RL demonstrates significant improvements in sample efficiency and stable performance over strong baselines through Q-learning and actor-critic algorithms.

problem: Infrared object detection is vulnerable to physical adversarial attacks where shape geometry is the primary information carrier, but shape-based methods face a trade-off between representational capability and optimization power.
approach: Leverage learnable Fourier shapes in end-to-end differentiable framework where compact Fourier coefficients analytically map to pixel-space masks via winding number theorem for efficient gradient-based optimization.
contribution: Physical patches achieve over 88% attack success rate at distances greater than 25m, demonstrating striking robustness across diverse distances, angles, poses, and individuals.

problem: Vision-language models suffer efficiency collapse when vision tokens dominate compute and memory, and prior token-reduction strategies trade off salience and diversity with limited hyperparameter robustness.
approach: SPLIT estimates token importance via temporal shifts of hidden states to avoid attention-score biases, assigns adaptive region-level budgets for localized coverage, and selects tokens via diversity score prioritizing distinctive representations.
contribution: SPLIT preserves over 99% accuracy with 192 vision tokens and 92.8% with only 64 tokens on image understanding with LLaVA-1.5-7B.

problem: Rapid face recognition dataset evaluation without full-scale training requires metrics to assess inherent potential, but existing approaches lack validation-free alternatives.
approach: Intrinsic Quality (IQ) integrates Neighbor-Consistency Score quantifying local identity label agreement and Global Representation Subspace Complexity (Effective Rank) capturing embedding geometry and dataset diversity.
contribution: IQ enables rapid evaluation using lightweight proxy models or data subsets, facilitating dataset diagnosis and curation prior to resource-intensive training.

problem: Multi-objective discrete optimization in domains like molecular design faces challenges with vast combinatorial spaces where closed-source LLMs cannot update parameters and smaller models lack broad knowledge.
approach: MCCE unites a frozen closed-source LLM with trainable model via progressive refinement through reinforcement learning, maintaining trajectory memory and enabling mutual support through joint exploration and experience-driven learning.
contribution: MCCE achieves state-of-the-art Pareto front quality on multi-objective drug design benchmarks, outperforming baselines through hybrid LLM collaboration.

problem: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) incurs prohibitive computational costs due to extensive group-based sampling, and selective data utilization methods risk inducing estimation bias.
approach: Dynamic Pruning Policy Optimization (DPPO) enables dynamic pruning while preserving unbiased gradient estimation through importance sampling-based correction, with Dense Prompt Packing to maximize token density.
contribution: DPPO achieves 2.37x training speedup on Qwen3-4B MATH tasks and outperforms GRPO by 3.36% average accuracy across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Strong universal Bayes-consistency for general metric losses lacks necessary and sufficient characterization in the realizable setting, extending only partially beyond classification and regression.
approach: Extend realizable Bayes-consistency theory by introducing infinite non-decreasing (γ_k)-Littlestone trees where γ_k tends to infinity, providing sharp characterization via combinatorial obstruction.
contribution: Resolve the realizable case of open problem in metric loss learning by establishing conditions under which distribution-free learning rules achieve near-optimal risk.

problem: Quantum error correction decoder deployment is hindered by a fundamental accuracy-latency tradeoff on microsecond timescales, requiring evaluation of neural decoder practical deployability.
approach: Unify representative neural decoders into five architectural paradigms and develop end-to-end compression pipeline to evaluate deployability on FPGA hardware for surface-code decoding up to distance d=9.
contribution: Reveal that near-term performance is driven by data scale over architecture complexity, appropriate inductive bias is essential, and INT4 quantization enables microsecond-scale FPGA latency.
